name: Nuclear plant safety
summary: Zaporizhzhia's off-site power remains fragile as Russian strikes hit Ukraine's grid
state: Substation damage has delayed the use of a repaired Zaporizhzhia power line, leaving the plant on fragile off-site power, according to IAEA updates (World Nuclear News; IAEA). Russia said it struck a 330kV substation in Dnipropetrovsk region on 5 Nov as attacks on Ukraine's energy system continue (Al Jazeera). No damage to safety systems or radiological release had been reported as of 6 Nov.
for_you: There is no radiation risk outside the area. Follow IAEA and national regulator updates; the UK government advises against all travel to Ukraine's occupied areas.
rubric_hit: Watch: off-site power fragile amid strikes on the grid; no safety-system damage

sources.title: World Nuclear News — Substation damage delaying operation of repaired Zaporizhzhia power line
IAEA — Update 354: Director General statement on situation in Ukraine

why: Fighting near nuclear power plants risks a radiological release; the IAEA reports on Zaporizhzhia and other plants in or near war zones.
drivers: Off-site power losses, strikes near plants, staffing, cooling water, military occupation.

rubric.alert: Damage to safety-critical systems, an INES level 2 or higher event, or a radiological release.
rubric.watch: A plant loses all off-site power, strikes land near a plant, or the IAEA reports a deteriorating safety situation.
rubric.normal: No new IAEA safety concerns at plants in or near conflict zones.
